purpose: The Engineering Assurance release this repository adopts, and the digest of the artifact it actually reads from that release. Component version pins are NOT restated here: the packaged compatibility matrix is their authority and a second copy would drift from it.
matrix_authority: engineering_assurance/compatibility-matrix.json in the installed distribution. scripts/check_shared_pins.py observes the local toolchain and delegates every verdict to engineering_assurance.compatibility.
registry: Every npm component resolves from the public npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). The internal npm.ix mirror must not appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc, and is not an oracle for whether a release landed. Querying an @agent-ix package needs --@agent-ix:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org; a bare --registry does not override the scoped .npmrc entry.

engineering_assurance.release_form: git tag v0.2.0, a source distribution; the tag is the released artifact

consumed_artifacts.why: The module scripts/check_shared_pins.py imports for every version verdict: classify_all, accepted and load_matrix all come from here. It replaces the four artifacts this repository used to pin, which were read only by the deleted retained-evidence compatibility view. A pin list with nothing live in it would leave check_shared_pins.py's digest check asserting over an empty population, which is a check that cannot fail rather than a check that passed.

The authority on which component versions are pinned. Deliberately carries no digest here: it is expected to advance as the matrix is re-accepted, and pinning its bytes locally would make this repository a second acceptance authority.

known_drift: engineering-assurance v0.2.0 packages compatibility-matrix.json with accepted.state = pending_human_acceptance and ships no human_acceptance_recorded predicate. Both landed on main after the tag (48daacd, ae50e13) and no v0.2.1 was cut. Filed as agent-ix/engineering-assurance#20. scripts/check_shared_pins.py reports the acceptance state the installed package records and gates only on the local toolchain, so an absent field is never read as an approval in either direction.

The human acceptance itself is not in doubt: Peter Krenesky accepted the FR-012 matrix on 2026-09-01 and it is attributed on engineering-assurance main as ae50e13. What is missing is a release carrying it. Pinning a branch head to obtain it is exactly what FR-012-AC-1 forbids, so this repository does not.

Kani emits no machine-readable result document. cargo kani prints a human transcript and returns a process status. scripts/run_kani_gate.py is therefore the domain tool that owns the transcript, and it is this repository's producer: it publishes runtime.kani-proof/v1, a declared structured result with a per-harness row and a discharged-obligation count. No downstream gate reads the transcript; every downstream gate reads a field. This is the 'no structured output exists' case the migration contract allows, and the domain tool is where the parsing lives.
